guide.summary: Museums, North Shore viewpoints and public markets, with breakfast spots, dinners, bakeries, coffee and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Check closing days before you plan: the Vancouver Art Gallery is closed on Tuesdays, the Museum of Anthropology at UBC is closed Mondays from October 15 to May 15, and The Polygon Gallery lists no Monday or Tuesday hours.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Vancouver Art Gallery is closed on Tuesdays, and the Museum of Anthropology at UBC is closed Mondays from October 15 to May 15. Vancouver Maritime Museum opens Tuesday to Sunday, and St. Lawrence serves Wednesday to Sunday only.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: The Vancouver Art Gallery recommends booking online to avoid the line, and Capilano Suspension Bridge Park says passholders must reserve online with limited weekend slots. Kissa Tanto releases Tock reservations 30 days in advance at midnight.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins and deals
toolkit.copy: Vij's says walk-in guests are always welcome, and The Keefer Bar keeps plenty of space for walk-ins. The Polygon Gallery is always by donation, and the Museum of Anthropology at UBC is half price on Thursdays after 5 pm.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: The Keefer Bar states guests must be 19+. Blue Water Cafe asks parties of 8 or more to contact it directly, and Kissa Tanto's largest table seats 6.

guide.dek: Pair one North Shore outing with a museum day downtown or at UBC, and check each venue's closing day before you commit.
intro: Vancouver rewards you for splitting your days between the city and the North Shore. Capilano Suspension Bridge Park at 3735 Capilano Road lists hours of 10 AM to 8 PM and asks passholders to reserve online, with limited weekend and holiday slots. Further up Nancy Greene Way, Grouse Mountain advertises newly opened Red Skyride cabins. Back on the water, Lonsdale Quay Market is open seven days a week, and The Polygon Gallery next door is always admission by donation, open Wednesday to Sunday with Thursdays until 9pm.

For museums, plan around closing days. The Vancouver Art Gallery on Hornby Street is closed on Tuesdays and stays open until 8 PM on Fridays; Future Geographies and SANCTUARY: The Ancient Forest Experience both run until January 10, 2027. The Museum of Anthropology at UBC is closed Mondays from October 15 to May 15, opens late on Thursdays until 9 pm at half price after 5 pm, and shows Tupananchiskama: Ancient Andean Cosmovision until January 3, 2027, with From the Deep opening November 19, 2026.

In Kitsilano, the Museum of Vancouver stays open until 8pm Thursday to Saturday, and the Vancouver Maritime Museum opens Tuesday to Sunday, with its St. Roch Revitalization listed as opening Winter 2026/2027. For a slower morning, the Granville Island Public Market opens 9 AM to 6 PM and closes on Mondays in January only. Purebread's Gastown branch opens daily from 8am, while Beaucoup Bakery's Kitsilano shop lists closures on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

Dinner needs some planning. Kissa Tanto on East Pender opens Tock reservations 30 days ahead at midnight, while Vij's on Cambie opens daily from 5:30 p.m. and says walk-in guests are always welcome. Published on Main says it is ranked #17 on North America's 50 Best Restaurants 2026, and Hawksworth runs a daily lounge-only cocktail hour from 4pm to 6pm. For a late drink, The Keefer Bar in Chinatown is open until 1am most nights and 2am on weekends, for guests 19 and over.
summaryCards: Pair the Vancouver Art Gallery (closed Tuesdays) with lunch at the Granville Island Public Market, then cross to Capilano Suspension Bridge Park.
Start with a pastry at Purebread in Gastown from 8am, then walk to Nemesis Coffee on West Hastings before the galleries open at 10.
Kissa Tanto releases tables 30 days ahead on Tock, Capilano passholders must reserve online, and The Keefer Bar admits guests 19 and over only.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Stanley Park (City of Vancouver), the Vancouver Aquarium and Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden returned HTTP 403; Bill Reid Gallery, 49th Parallel, Revolver, Anh and Chi and Elysian Coffee returned HTTP 429; Science World, Vancouver Lookout, FlyOver Canada and Matchstick Coffee returned no readable content, so none of these are included, and none of these failures indicates a closure. Several confirmed places publish no dated 2026 content and rest on standing hours or booking notices (Joe Fortes, Miku, Café Medina, St. Lawrence, Botanist, The Pourhouse, Purebread, Beaucoup Bakery, Small Victory, Nemesis Coffee, Lonsdale Quay Market); Grouse Mountain, Café Medina and Published on Main publish no hours on the pages read; The Pourhouse shows two conflicting hour sets; and Beaucoup Bakery's Kitsilano hours are ambiguous in the page layout. The Diamond's former domain now redirects to another business. One automated summary of the Lonsdale Quay page mentioned AI-directed text, but a re-read found none, so nothing is quoted.
